name: Tunisia
sources: GDP $12.29bn and population 8,324,509 (World Bank, NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990).

Interest rate 11.5% is the Banque Centrale de Tunisie money-market rate under the administered ceilings of the 1987 structural adjustment programme. The World Bank publishes no deposit or lending series for Tunisia in 1990, so this figure is an estimate and is listed as unverified.
Military 1.84% of GDP (World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS, 1990). Bourguiba kept the army small and out of politics on purpose; Ben Ali, a general, did not enlarge it.
External debt 64.72% of GNI (World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, 1990).
Tax revenue 19.95% of GDP (World Bank GC.TAX.TOTL.GD.ZS, 1990).
Gross fixed capital formation 24.36% of GDP (World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, 1990), split 0.10 state / 0.14 private.
Oil about 0.10 mbd from El Borma and the offshore Ashtart field (EIA international series, 1990) — enough to matter to the budget, not enough to make Tunisia a producer.

Authoritarianism 0.74: the Rassemblement Constitutionnel Democratique took every one of the 141 seats in the Chamber of Deputies on 2 April 1989 under a winner-take-all list system, and Ennahda was refused legal registration and then broken up in 1991.
Stability 63. Ben Ali's 1987 removal of Bourguiba was constitutional in form and bloodless, and the economy was growing; the pressure came from an Islamist movement with no legal route.
Separatism 0.02. Tunisia is the most homogeneous state in the region.
Military strength 3, just above Kuwait's 2: 35,000 men, no armour worth the name, and a doctrine of not fighting anyone.
